newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH Q4 ENGINEERING ORDERS FALL 23 PCT - MET.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH Q4 ENGINEERING ORDERS FALL 23 PCT - MET.

text.p: The value of new orders won by the Finnish machinery and metal products industry fell 23 percent yr/yr in Q4, the Confederation of Metal, Engineering and Electrotechnical Industries (MET) said on Tuesday.

"The domestic forest industry's big investments are coming to a halt, that is why we think it is natural that fewer new orders have recently been booked by the machinery and metal products industry," MET director Timo Airaksinen told a news conference.

The value of the machinery and metal products industry's -- excluding shipbuilding -- export orders fell three percent yr/yr in October-December and the value of domestic orders was 50 percent lower, he said.
The sector's order backlog at end-1996 corresponded to the output of roughly seven months -- down eight percent from the beginning of October, Airaksinen said.
The business cycle in the machinery and metal products industry is expected to improve in the second half of 1997, he said.
"This is mainly based on improving export prospects and on expectations that a forecast economic upturn in Europe will materialise," he said.
